bibliographic.title: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges
bibliographic.authors: Ranjan Sapkota, Konstantinos I. Roumeliotis, Manoj Karkee
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sapkota, R., Roumeliotis, K. I., & Karkee, M. (2025). AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges. Information Fusion. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.inffus.2025.103599

methodology.method_family: conceptual taxonomy review with stated search strategy
methodology.study_design: structured conceptual review comparing AI Agents and Agentic AI across architectural evolution, operational mechanisms, interaction styles, and autonomy levels
methodology.sector: multi-domain including customer support, research automation, robotics, and medical decision support
methodology.technology_context: LLMs, LIMs, generative AI, AI Agents, Agentic AI, multi-agent systems, RAG, ReAct loops, tool integration, prompt engineering

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a conceptual review distinguishing AI Agents from Agentic AI through taxonomy, application mapping, and challenge analysis. The provided text shows strong relevance to LLMs, agents, RAG, explainability, and some regulated-adjacent domains such as medical decision support, but it does not center conversational governance, compliance controls, human oversight mechanisms, auditability, or governance frameworks for regulated conversational systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: The abstract and introduction support inclusion as foundational context, but the excerpt does not show the full search strategy, governance-specific sections, or depth of regulated-domain analysis needed to confirm supporting versus central status.

appraisal.notes: Objective and taxonomy framing are clear in the abstract and introduction. The text states that a search strategy is outlined, but the provided excerpt does not include enough methodological detail to judge sampling adequacy, screening procedures, or limitation reporting.

cerqual.explanation: The conceptual distinction between AI Agents and Agentic AI is coherent and clearly presented, but the excerpt offers limited transparency on review methods and only partial relevance to conversational governance in regulated environments.

coding.theme: Conceptual distinction between AI Agents and Agentic AI
coding.subtheme: Taxonomy, applications, and challenges in the generative AI era
rq_alignment: partial alignment via explainability and regulated-adjacent healthcare applications
limited direct alignment with conversational governance and compliance controls

synthesis.main_claim: AI Agents and Agentic AI are divergent paradigms that require distinct taxonomies, architectures, and capability assessments in the generative AI era.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured conceptual taxonomy, application mapping, and comparative analysis of opportunities and challenges across AI Agents and Agentic AI, including proposed solutions such as RAG and ReAct loops.
synthesis.limitations: The provided excerpt does not include sufficient detail on the search strategy, corpus size, screening criteria, or governance-specific analysis for regulated conversational systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for defining and distinguishing LLM-enabled agent paradigms, related architectural mechanisms such as RAG, and high-level risks like hallucination; not sufficient as central evidence for conversational governance in regulated environments based on the text provided.
